scope: Frozen-critic actor-gradient diagnosis, native weighted FM; known optimizer baselines, not a new reward or official RECAP reproduction
sampling: Freeze shared critic seed0 top64 scheduled draws/task from completed critic-signal study. Uniform task-balanced deterministic cycling four times,2A+2B every batch,512 effective supervised draws. Original retained occurrences and labels unchanged; fresh per-cycle flow noise, paired across modes; noise/zero-adapter initialization vary only by actor seed. This is a new matched ordinary baseline, not the earlier sparse128-supervision policy.
task_gradients: One task per microbatch. Capture each backward contribution after official FSDP context, clear gradients between tasks, combine in FP32, restore original parameter dtypes. Guard with4-step exact native-accumulation replay before main training.
balance: If both tasks nonzero, rescale each entire shared trainable gradient to their mean L2 norm, then sum. Zero-task gradients are not conflicts and do not halve the active task.
pcgrad: For two tasks with negative dot, project each original task gradient onto the normal plane of the other, then sum; same global coefficients on adapter and expert, not blockwise projection.
magnitude_control: For nondegenerate interventions rescale combined raw gradient to the ordinary combined raw L2 norm. Keep existing separate adapter/expert clip1 and official FP32MasterAdamW. Degenerate zero sums stay zero and are logged. This does not force equal actual AdamW steps; measure actual parameter deltas and first-order task effects separately.
evaluation: Fixed final128 only, original12 development scenes per task, same noise/checker, each of9 actors evaluated on both tasks; no checkpoint selection
limits: Two tasks/three paired actor seeds, fixed critic and selected data; negative cosine or local linear loss change is not proof of negative transfer. Task-grouped updates do not establish language grounding. Actual-step magnitude remains a possible mediator.
